key_cases.court: Supreme Court of the United States
key_cases.holding: The Supreme Court held that the Adoption Assistance and Child Welfare Act's requirement that states make reasonable efforts to prevent removal and reunify families creates no right enforceable by private individuals under section 1983 or directly under the Act.
key_cases.relevance: It confirms that federally required oversight structures do not themselves confer private rights.
key_cases.quote: We hold that the Act does not create an enforceable right on behalf of respondents.

key_cases.case_name: Georgia Department of Human Services, Division of Family and Children Services v. Steiner
key_cases.holding: The Supreme Court of Georgia reversed the superior court and upheld the central child abuse registry as applied, holding that listing as a substantiated abuser did not, on this record, satisfy the stigma-plus test and so triggered no federal procedural due process protection, and that 'some evidence' supported the ALJ's substantiation.
key_cases.relevance: It shows that review of Georgia substantiation decisions runs through an ALJ and the courts, not a citizen panel.
key_cases.quote: Steiner failed to demonstrate a constitutionally protected liberty or property interest sufficient to trigger the due process protections that he claims were violated by operation of the registry
